issues.issue: This paragraph requires 'the parties specified on Exhibit V' to deliver Form 8-K Disclosure Information, while Section 9.12(c)(i) says that information 'shall be reported by the parties set forth on Exhibit S hereto.' Which exhibit identifies the reporting parties is stated two ways.

The subsection breaks off mid-sentence at 'not resulting from its own negligence, bad faith or 107 of', leaving the exception to the liability disclaimer incomplete. The limit of the Trust Administrator's exculpation for late filings is unstated.

The outside date is 'the Latest Possible Maturity Date as defined in the Preliminary Statement,' but that term is defined in Section 1.01 by a formula and the Preliminary Statement merely tabulates December 25, 2046. Which date caps the trust's existence depends on which source controls.

The auction may proceed only if the price suffices to retire 'each class of notes issued pursuant to the Indenture' and amounts owed to 'the trustee under the Indenture,' but no Indenture is defined or identified anywhere in this Agreement. A condition to any Auction Sale is expressed by reference to an instrument the Agreement does not supply.

This subsection conditions the Master Servicer's purchase right on non-exercise by 'a Majority in Interest of the Class C Certificateholders, as Auction Initiator,' whereas Auction Initiator is defined as 'the Class C Certificateholder' and, failing its exercise, the Certificate Insurer. Whose inaction unlocks the Master Servicer's right is stated differently in the two places.

The Termination Price rests on an appraisal 'mutually agreed upon by the Master Servicer and the Trust Administrator' and a fair market value 'determined by the Master Servicer and the Trust Administrator,' although the parties clause makes Wells Fargo both. The apparent two-party check on the purchase price collapses into one entity valuing the assets it is buying.

Unsurrendered final distributions are paid over to UBS Securities LLC, a non-party, and 'all rights of non-tendering Certificateholders in or to such amounts shall thereupon cease hereunder, under the related Certificates and, if applicable, under the Certificate Insurance Policy,' while the Policy provides that it sets forth Financial Security's undertaking in full and cannot be modified or affected by any other agreement. Whether the PSA can extinguish a Holder's rights against the insurer is a question between the two instruments.

Clause (v) permits amendment without Certificateholder consent 'to modify, alter, amend, add to or rescind any of the terms or provisions contained in this Agreement,' subject only to an opinion of no material adverse effect that is deemed satisfied by rating agency letters, while the later paragraph of Section 11.01 requires the consent of a Majority in Interest of each affected Class for changes to Holders' rights. The open-ended power in clause (v) would swallow the consent requirement.

The provision refers to the Form 10-K 'and the Certification required to be attached thereto as referenced in Section 9.12(d),' but the certification requirement is in Section 9.12(b)(iv) and Section 9.12(d) deals with Form 15 and late or amended filings. The amendment power is defined by a broken cross-reference.

The opening words require the consent of 'the Holders of a Majority in Interest of each Class of Certificates affected thereby,' i.e. 51%, while clause (ii) requires consent of Holders of 'Percentage Interests aggregating 66%' of an adversely affected Class for the same kind of amendment. The governing consent threshold is stated twice at different levels.

The opinion condition applies to every amendment 'other than pursuant to the second preceding paragraph,' a reference whose target depends on how the long preceding paragraphs of Section 11.01 are counted. Which class of amendments escapes the opinion requirement is indeterminate.
